dossier.public_summary: The dip’s depth jumps from ~1600 ppm to ~14,000 ppm between sectors and between individual transits, with the signal only appearing strongly in two events, unlike a steady planetary transit. Two similar but faint neighbours nearby could mimic the signal with eclipses, so a blended eclipsing binary is the best explanation, not a planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes by an order of magnitude within the same SPOC source, not a calibration offset. A planet on the target must be steady; highly variable depth implies blended/background eclipsing binary or systematic drive, positively favoring EB over planet.

reasons.why: Signal is driven by two very deep transits only, not seen consistently, with no planet-like on-target depth. Combined with required wide eclipses from neighbours far from the pixel, best explanation is a blend/variable depth from contamination, not a 3.141 Rearth planet on the M dwarf (0.3457 Rsol).
